Playbook:
Description: How to read terminal output from ``execute_script`` / ``write_script`` and optional env tuning.
Terminal format: - Output merges **stdout**, then **[stderr]** if present, then metadata like ``[exit_code=N]``. - ``exit_code=0`` means success; any other code is a real failure — diagnose before retrying. - ``[running=true]`` or ``[timed_out=true]`` means the command may still be running in the **shared PTY**; do not assume success from partial output. - ``(no output)`` means the command produced nothing visible.
Timeouts (optional env): - ``GENCYBER_DEFAULT_CMD_TIMEOUT`` — default seconds for ordinary commands (often 60). - ``GENCYBER_LONG_CMD_TIMEOUT`` — use a higher budget yourself for long scans (nmap, gobuster, hashcat, etc.) by keeping the command focused or splitting work; the tool default is the short timeout unless you pass ``command_timeout`` in state. - ``GENCYBER_WRITE_SCRIPT_TIMEOUT`` — max seconds for the remote write step (default 120).
Scripts on disk: - ``write_script`` saves under ``GENCYBER_AGENT_SCRIPT_DIR`` (default ``/workspace/.gencyber-agent-scripts``). - Supported extensions: ``py``, ``sh``, ``bash`` (and similar short names). Next turn: ``command`` = ``python3 /path/to/file.py`` or ``bash /path/to/file.sh``. - Never use a giant ``python3 -c '...'`` one-liner for multi-line logic — use ``write_script`` then run the saved path.
Shared shell: - One persistent PTY per session; cwd and env persist across turns. - If a prior command failed, change approach (fix paths, permissions, syntax) — do not repeat the same failing command unchanged.
